import os
import sys

import pytest

import click
from click.testing import CliRunner

needs_fd_capture = pytest.mark.skipif(
    sys.platform == "win32",
    reason="fd capture not supported on Windows",
)


def test_capture_default_is_sys():
    """The default ``capture`` mode is ``sys`` when not specified."""
    runner = CliRunner()
    assert runner.capture == "sys"


@needs_fd_capture
def test_capture_fd_system_exit_nonzero():
    """fd-captured output is preserved even when the command exits with a
    non-zero status via ``SystemExit``."""

    @click.command()
    def cli():
        os.write(1, b"before exit\n")
        click.echo("before echo exit")
        raise SystemExit(3)

    runner = CliRunner(capture="fd")
    result = runner.invoke(cli)
    assert result.exit_code == 3
    assert "before exit" in result.stdout
    assert "before echo exit" in result.stdout


@needs_fd_capture
def test_capture_fd_uncaught_exception_restores_fds():
    """When ``catch_exceptions=False`` lets an exception propagate, fd
    capture must still be torn down so later invocations work normally."""

    @click.command()
    def failing_cli():
        os.write(1, b"partial output\n")
        raise RuntimeError("boom")

    runner = CliRunner(capture="fd")
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="boom"):
        runner.invoke(failing_cli, catch_exceptions=False)

    # The fd redirection must have been torn down; a subsequent invocation
    # using fd capture should work normally and not fail or hang.
    @click.command()
    def ok_cli():
        os.write(1, b"fd ok\n")
        click.echo("py ok")

    result = runner.invoke(ok_cli)
    assert result.exit_code == 0
    assert "fd ok" in result.stdout
    assert "py ok" in result.stdout


@needs_fd_capture
def test_capture_fd_caught_exception_still_captures_output():
    """With ``catch_exceptions=True`` (the default), output written before
    the exception is still captured and the exception is reported on the
    result object rather than raised."""

    @click.command()
    def failing_cli():
        os.write(1, b"fd before failure\n")
        click.echo("py before failure")
        raise RuntimeError("kaboom")

    runner = CliRunner(capture="fd")
    result = runner.invoke(failing_cli)
    assert result.exit_code == 1
    assert isinstance(result.exception, RuntimeError)
    assert "fd before failure" in result.stdout
    assert "py before failure" in result.stdout


@needs_fd_capture
def test_capture_fd_empty_output():
    """A command that writes nothing produces empty streams without error."""

    @click.command()
    def cli():
        pass

    runner = CliRunner(capture="fd")
    result = runner.invoke(cli)
    assert result.exit_code == 0
    assert result.stdout == ""
    assert result.stderr == ""


def test_capture_invalid_mode_message_lists_choices():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="sys' or 'fd"):
        CliRunner(capture="bogus")  # type: ignore[arg-type]
